main_issue: Whether and when strong-smelling cooking (D's fried salted fish) is allowed in the shared flat; resolved as Saturdays only with a heads-up from D.

A-B.evidence: A wanted a full ban (1); B proposed no ban, window, heads-up, and evening cooking (2, 6). A proposed Saturdays (7), B put it to D and confirmed it (8, 10), and A said 'that works for me' (14).

A-C.evidence: C wanted a heads-up so laundry could be brought in (3), which differs from A's ban. C then said 'Saturdays are fine with me' (11), and A agreed to the plan (14). They never addressed each other directly.

A-D.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (1), while D cooks it twice a week and agreed only to a heads-up (4). D then accepted Saturdays (9), and A accepted that (7, 14). A's Saturday idea was addressed to D through B.

B-C.evidence: C backed B's heads-up idea (3). B restated the Saturday plan (10) and C said Saturdays are fine (11).

B-D.evidence: D accepted B's heads-up (4). B asked D about Saturdays (8), D agreed (9), and D confirmed the heads-up (12).

C-D.evidence: Both supported the heads-up (3, 4), and both accepted Saturdays (9, 11). They did not address each other directly.
